items.response:
That's a lot to absorb: your one protected morning got taken, then a day trip lands on top of an already stacked week, and once again you're the one flexing. Being worn out by that makes complete sense.
Action: I'll leave the opinions out and just line up Toronto-Montreal options for Thu the 8th, out in the morning and back in time for dinner, and show them to you before booking anything.

Posting the Slack message now. Tom's favourite is single-malt Scotch, specifically Lagavulin; my note has the 16 at about $150 at LCBO, so that price may have moved.
Action: Post the #payouts-launch message, and check the current LCBO price and stock for Lagavulin 16 before buying. The note about collecting contributors over $100 was for the team card, so tell me if this bottle is just from you.

Added: Leo's swim lessons, every Tuesday at 5:30 pm at the Pam McConnell Aquatic Centre in Regent Park, starting tomorrow.
Action: Create the recurring event and confirm once it's on the calendar.

Good news that he can make it Monday. I don't have the crew's contact or their working hours in front of me, so I'll find them in your contacts and reno notes rather than guess.
Action: Find who to reach on the kitchen crew, then draft a text saying the electrician is coming Monday and asking what time works for them, and show it to you before sending.

Five nut-free ideas: ham and cheese pinwheels with cucumber sticks, pasta salad with cheese cubes, mini bagel pizzas, chicken quesadilla strips with mild salsa, and a yogurt tube with crackers and fruit. Check labels every time, since the family keeps all nuts out of his lunches, no exceptions. I don't have what you asked me about Biscuit and the ambulance, so I won't guess.
Action: Search our earlier conversations for that question and the answer, and give you Leo's version once I've found it.

So far this morning: I added Felipe the dog walker to the pet budget ($50/week, which puts monthly pet spend at about $729 against the $350 budget), and I built the 'Payouts v2 launch risks (2025-11-12)' Notion page with 6 risks for tomorrow's standup. The October grocery total from the TD accounts, plus August and September for comparison, is still being pulled.
Action: Send you the grocery comparison as soon as it's back.

On it, checking the holds on your card ending 4417 at Pape/Danforth and Leslieville. Tom's message can wait until after dinner, so I'll leave it alone.
Action: List which holds are ready with pickup-by dates, plus anything due this week that can be renewed, and note if one branch lets you do it all in one trip.

Texting Nate only, no calls, to ask whether the cabinets are still arriving Monday. My notes had the delivery down as Thu 16 Oct, 8:00-10:00, with someone home to let the crew in, so I'll mention that so he knows which date I mean. I'll also gather his invoices, starting with #NR-2207 ($6,500, due Fri 3 Oct).
Action: Send the text, then search your email for all Northline invoices, add them to the reno sheet and tell you if any are missing.

Done: Jess from Rover walks Biscuit at noon on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays, starting Monday. That's $75 a week at $25 a walk. Monday is also cabinet delivery morning (8-10, Nate on site from 7:30), but Jess comes after that.
Action: Add the recurring Mon/Wed/Fri 12:00 event starting Monday and add Jess's walks to the pet budget at $25 x 3 per week.

Yes, I'll put it together for Tanvi: a 2010 condo is covered by rent control, so the 2026 cap is the 2.1% guideline and anything above that needs LTB approval. The landlord must give 90 days' written notice on Form N1, only once every 12 months, and if she gets an N1 for 9% with no LTB application she can simply pay the guideline amount.
Action: Write it up as a short note with links to the official Ontario sources and send it to you to forward to her.

Will do. I'll put Nate's revised quote next to the $48,000 budget; that figure includes a 10% contingency, so I'll work out how much of it the quote is already using.
Action: Pull the revised quote from your email, compare it line by line to the budget, and have the contingency check ready for after your review.

Two is a very reasonable number, and no regrets is the right review for a custard tart. Hope the coat-weather AC lets you enjoy them in peace.
Action: None needed.

Happy to, but I don't have a record of which topics you keep missing, so I don't want to guess at your weak spots. If you tell me the one or two areas, I'll build the 8-10 questions around them.
Action: Check our earlier practice notes for your trouble spots; if there's nothing, start a mixed warm-up quiz and adapt to your first few answers.

I'd rather not guess at your exact title on a benefits form at 10pm. I'll find it in your HR profile or email signature and draft the areas of responsibility in a couple of lines.
Action: Look up your official title and send you a short responsibilities blurb to paste in tonight.

Lately it's been couch-cushion forts, and Biscuit has taken over the latest one. Beyond that I don't have a current list of what he's into, and I don't have his food restrictions in front of me, so I won't guess on either for Grace.
Action: Check your notes for Leo's interests and any food restrictions, then draft a reply you can send to Grace.

Living without a working kitchen and with dust everywhere would wear anyone down, and wanting your toast back is completely fair. For the floors: skip the broom, vacuum with a soft brush head (beater bar off), then go over it with a dry microfiber mop and finish with a barely damp one, since wet dust turns into a film.
Action: I'm here to keep talking; if it would help, I can also lay out a concrete plan for the next few weeks, just say so.

¡Claro! Quiz rápido, escribe el o la: 1) ___ sistema, 2) ___ día, 3) ___ tema, 4) ___ foto, 5) ___ planeta, 6) ___ radio, 7) ___ idioma, 8) ___ clima. Mándame tus respuestas y te corrijo, y en la ronda dos hacemos problema, mapa y mano.
Action: Score your answers as they come in and keep the sync with Aisha and Diego as booked.

Pulling them up now: I'll list this month's notes by date and title so you can see the whole mess at once. I won't change or delete anything until you say how you want them sorted.
Action: List this month's personal notes, then propose a grouping for you to approve.

I'd hold off on sending a yes. My notes say Leo doesn't do well with sleepovers yet and that he's in bed at 7:45 on school nights, so pizza, a movie and a night at Hannah's could go badly. How about a polite no to the sleepover with an offer instead, like Jun coming to ours, or Leo joining for pizza and being picked up before bedtime?
Action: Draft a warm text to Hannah for your approval and leave the family calendar alone until you decide.

Sending the Hannah text now. For Olivia's blurb I don't have the Instant Payouts v1 scope in front of me, so I'll pull it from the PRD and launch notes rather than invent features.
Action: Send Hannah the playground and market text, then draft a 4-5 line v1 blurb for Olivia's deck and show it to you.

A beagle snore that gets mistaken for drilling is a real talent. Hope Diego enjoyed the sound effects.
Action: None needed.

Poor Leo, I'm sorry about the tooth. Dr. Lin is at Danforth Smiles, 822 Danforth Ave, and Leo's regular checkup there isn't until Tue 3 Nov at 8:45 am, which is too far off for a chipped front tooth. I'll ask for the earliest after-school slot this week and work out the travel time from home.
Action: Contact Danforth Smiles (416-555-0182) for an urgent after-school appointment this week, work out the door-to-door travel time from home, and bring you the options before confirming.

I don't have a confirmed GA date for Instant Payouts in what I have, and I don't want to put an unconfirmed date in front of a sales deck. I'll check the GA milestone and draft the note with whatever is actually committed.
Action: Look up the GA date in Linear and Notion, draft a short note to Olivia that states it (and whether it's committed), and show it to you before sending.

Yesterday's route isn't in what I have, so I won't quote a drive time from memory. I'll find it and compare the estimate with how long it actually felt, including any stops you made.
Action: Search yesterday's conversation and your maps history for the route and its estimated time, and report both.

Holding the order. I don't have a saved inventory of the basement kitchen setup, so I'll check your reno notes rather than list gear from memory.
Action: Search your notes for the basement kitchen setup and send back a short list of what you have plus a few easy meals that fit it, with the order on hold until you talk to Sam.

Pickup in store works, so I'll set that up at Queen & Logan for Sam. Here's a draft for the payouts team: 'Quick reminder: release freeze runs Thu 12:00 to Mon 09:00 for the bank-partner cutover. Please get anything you need merged by Thursday morning. Thanks all!'
Action: Set up the store pickup in Sam's name and save the Slack draft in #payouts-launch without posting it.

I'll pull up the reno notes and look for the reasons you recorded for choosing Nate; I don't want to reconstruct them from memory and give Sam the wrong story. If the notes don't cover it, the original quotes in email might.
Action: Open the reno notes, summarise why Nate was picked over the other two contractors, and draft a short reply for Sam.

Asking Olivia to move QBR prep to 11:00 on Thu Mar 5 so it clears the roadmap check-in. For Ellie's dairy allergy I don't have a pantry inventory, so I'll check recent grocery orders rather than guess, and flag anything that needs a label check.
Action: Message Olivia with the 11:00 request, and send you a short list of dairy-free snacks we likely have, noting what to label-check before the kids get home.

Sorry about the bag wait and the missing swim shirt and stuffie. I don't have your packing method saved, so I won't guess at it; could you remind me how you want it done?
Action: Start a trip-home packing list with Leo's swim shirt and stuffie at the top, and reshape it to your method once you tell me what it is.

I'll look up Environment Canada's record for Ottawa on Sunday the 25th and give it to you in Celsius and metric units only, with wind in km/h and snow in cm.
Action: Pull the observed high and low, snowfall, wind and wind chill for that day so you can settle it with Grace.

Will do: I'll end your out-of-office tomorrow morning and swap the message to something like 'Hi, I'm back but still catching up, so replies may be a little slow. Best, Riya'.
Action: Update the auto-reply text, set it to end tomorrow morning at the start of your workday (tell me an exact time if you want one), and confirm.

I'll pull the all-hands email up and boil it down to the four things that actually matter for you.
Action: Find this afternoon's all-hands email, read it, and send you four bullets with any dates or actions that touch your work.

Ugh, sorry, that's a nasty one with no note left. The car is insured with Belairdirect now (policy BD-AU-7731904) rather than Intact, so the claim goes there. Before I file, I want to check your deductible, since a scratch and dent from an unknown driver may cost less to fix than the deductible and that's your call.
Action: Open the policy documents in Drive under Household > Car > Insurance for the deductible and claims steps, ask you for photos of the damage, and file the claim once you confirm.

That's a big deal and worth saying out loud: your first project led end to end as a senior PM, and it worked. Congratulations, you earned this.
Action: Save a note on the Instant Payouts launch (May 2026) so the details are ready for your next review, unless you'd rather I didn't.

Happy to. One thing to check first: my notes have Leo's Riverdale Farm day camp as Weeks 2 and 3, Jul 13-24, 9:00-16:00, not a Jun 29 start, so is Jun 29 a different camp or did the dates move? Either way the label-everything list starts with a hat, sunscreen, water bottle, lunch bag, a change of clothes and closed-toe shoes.
Action: Pull the camp's own packing list from the confirmation email, build the checklist from it, and check that the balance due 1 Jun went through.

Good plan on trying her cousin; tell me what you hear. For Priya, a few that fit an architect who bikes everywhere: Cabbagetown (the best-preserved Victorian streets, a short ride to the core), the Annex (big old houses and the Bloor bike lane), Little Portugal / Trinity Bellwoods (rowhouses with Dundas and Ossington bike lanes), and Corktown / Distillery if she wants converted lofts.
Action: Turn this into a short comparison with bike times to downtown once I know where her office will be.

Sending the school council reply now. For the car insurance: your Mazda is with Intact and renews each April, and I'd typically start collecting quotes about 4-6 weeks before renewal. Switching at renewal is usually simple, but I want to read your Intact terms for the exact notice and have the new policy start the same day so there's no gap.
Action: Send the school council reply, pull the Intact renewal letter for the exact renewal date and cancellation terms, and set a reminder for when to start quotes.

Fun combo to plan. For the sync opener, try a one-minute round where everyone shares one small win from the week, or a high and a low. For the evening, something low-effort at home: a pizza and movie night, or a board-game night with good snacks.
Action: Tell me which day and I'll add the opener to the sync agenda and block the evening on your calendar.

Checking Sam's text now. With only a microwave, the induction hotplate and the old fridge downstairs, I'd skip cooking tonight and go for takeout or something that only needs the microwave.
Action: Read Sam's message, then suggest two or three takeout options that fit what he said and order once you pick.

On it. I'll build the cart with all twelve items: milk, eggs, bread, rice, pasta, bananas, apples, yogurt tubes, cheddar, dish soap, paper towels and Sam's frozen veggie dumplings. The Sandbanks permit stays paused until you and Sam decide on PEC; weekend permits usually sell out by Thursday evening.
Action: Build the grocery cart, send you the total and the delivery or pickup slot to confirm, and leave the Sandbanks hold paused.

Sorry, dropping calls is miserable. I'll check for a known outage in your area first, then open the ticket with your provider.
Action: Find your provider and account details from your bills, check the outage status, and open a ticket noting the dropped calls this afternoon and asking for a fix before the weekend; I'll send you the ticket number.

COUNTIF is enough: =COUNTIF(D:D,">10000") counts the payouts over $10,000. If any amounts are stored as text they won't be counted, so check that column is formatted as numbers. Also, your two library holds are at Pape/Danforth, which closes at 20:30 tonight.
Action: Keep the library pickup on tonight's list; they're held until Saturday if you run out of time.

Noted: no replacement for the 2019 Mazda CX-5 in 2026, the money goes toward the kitchen renovation, and you'll revisit buying an EV in 2028. I'll get you off the dealer's lists.
Action: Find the dealer's emails, use their unsubscribe links, send an opt-out request covering any other marketing, and save the decision (with a 2028 EV revisit) to your car notes.

¡Aquí va, completo! 'Tres tristes tigres tragaban trigo en un trigal. En tres tristes trastos, tragaban trigo tres tristes tigres.' Start slow and speed up, and watch Carlos's face at 'trastos'. And dreading Sunday night before launch week is very normal; happy to sketch the week so it feels smaller.
Action: Give you a harder twister if you want one, or map out launch week whenever you're ready.

A dinosaur trip for just the two of you is a great march break plan. I'll look at 3-night hotel options in Drumheller for the week of the 16th and check Tyrrell ticket pricing for Leo, which depends on his age bracket, so I'll confirm that from your notes rather than guess.
Action: Search Drumheller hotels for 3 nights that week (I'll ask which nights if unclear), pull Tyrrell admission prices for a child, and send you options before booking anything.
